best_for: Windows users on low-RAM laptops and older PCs who want to watch memory use from the tray and free cached memory by hand before a heavy task.

points.title: What it clears
points.text: Mem Reduct trims the system and process working sets and empties the standby and modified page lists. The author puts the typical result at 10 to 50% of memory, and it varies by machine.

points.title: Relies on undocumented Windows calls
points.text: The cleaning uses internal Native API functions that Microsoft does not document. That is how it reaches the standby list, but behavior can change between Windows releases.

points.title: Needs administrator rights
points.text: The project says it needs admin rights to work correctly, and the installer here sets it up for all users on x64.

points.title: Portable if you want it
points.text: Put a `memreduct.ini` file next to the program, or move the one from `%APPDATA%\Henry++\Mem Reduct`, and it keeps its settings in its own folder.

points.title: Free, signed, Windows only
points.text: It is GPLv3 and supports Windows 7 through 11 on 64-bit and Arm64. Releases carry a GPG signature you can check. There is no Mac or Linux version, and the Windows listing keeps 3 versions.
